```{r Data download, include=FALSE}
if (!file.exists("../pci_data.csv")) {
  stop("NCR dataset not found! Please check that you have a single CSV file named \"pci_data.csv\" in the current directory!",
       call. = FALSE)
}

#Load in the helper functions/data required
source("../utilities/utilities.R")

#Read in data from PowerBI
pci_data_raw <- readr::read_csv("../pci_data.csv")
# pci_data <- readr::read_csv("./pci_data.csv", col_types = colTypes)
```

```{r Report context setup, include=FALSE}
target_po <- params$target_po
period_start <- params$period_start
period_end <- params$period_end
```

```{r replace_po_column, include=FALSE}
pci_data <- pci_data_raw |>
  dplyr::select(-po) |>
  merge(
    po_fixed |> 
      dplyr::select(ANGIOPLASTY_ID, po_fixed) |>
      dplyr::rename(po = po_fixed),
    by = "ANGIOPLASTY_ID",
    all.x = TRUE,
    sort = FALSE
  )
```


```{r Data transformation, include=FALSE}
pci_data <- prepare_pci_data(pci_data) |>
  # Format the Procedure Operator Name
  dplyr::left_join(
    wa_pci_operators |> 
      dplyr::select(CardiobaseIdentifier, PCIOperatorName) |> 
      dplyr::rename(po = CardiobaseIdentifier, po_name = PCIOperatorName),
    by = "po"
  ) |>
  # Create Count column for Number of PCI
  dplyr::mutate(
    count_pci = 1
  ) |>
  # Add comparison_group based on selected targeted clinician
  dplyr::mutate(
    comparison_group = factor(
      dplyr::if_else(po_name == target_po, "Your Data", "Other Clinicians"),
      levels = c("Your Data", "Other Clinicians")
    )
  ) |>
  # Multiple los columns for mean and median
  dplyr::mutate(
    los_mean = los,
    los_median = los
  ) |>
  # Filter for period start and period end for this report
  dplyr::filter(
    dop >= params$period_start & dop <= params$period_end
  )

# Filter for listed PCI operator last names if available
if (exists("wa_pci_operators")) {
  pci_data <- pci_data |>
    dplyr::filter(
      po %in% wa_pci_operators$CardiobaseIdentifier
    )
}
if (params$period_frequency == "quarterly") {
  pci_data <- pci_data |>
    # Change period_end to be quarterly instead
    dplyr::mutate(
      period_start = lubridate::quarter(period_end, type = "date_first"),
      period_end = lubridate::quarter(period_end, type = "date_last")
    )
}
```

# Introduction

This report details metrics and indicators for PCI procedures that you have performed (presented as “Your Data” in this report) within centres that are currently participating in data collection for the National Cardiac Registry (NCR). This report is confidential and is only available to you and your Head of Department.

The report displays your PCI metrics with a comparison to all other PCI operators in Western Australia for whom data are available. PCI are allocated to the first consultant listed within the procedure record. Indicator definitions and a detailed explanation on the charts used in this report can be found in the Appendix.

The data for this report is collected from the PCI Database of WA which is part of the Cardiac Registry of Western Australia (CRoWA). The Database was established to collect data from clinicians at the time of PCI and following hospital discharge. The PCI module of CRoWA builds upon the Database, improving the mapping of PCI quality indicators and data collection by gathering missing data from existing electronic sources.

Additional useful resources: [National Cardiac Registry 2025 Annual Report](https://nationalcardiacregistry.org.au/2025-annual-status-report/), [PCI Database of WA REDCap](https://datalibrary-rc.health.wa.gov.au), PCI Database of WA Data Definitions [TBC], [Cardiovascular Dashboard](https://app.powerbi.com/groups/me/apps/69877d7f-3ac7-449c-939d-18aa3e549a1a), Link to your PCI Reports [TBC].

# `r paste0("Summary (Current Reporting Period; ", short_current_start_date, " to ", short_current_end_date, ")")`

Below is a summary of your activity, during this reporting period, compared with all PCI operators within WA for whom data are available.

```{r last_period_summary, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Create table that summarises key metrics from the last period available
last_period_start <- max(pci_data$period_start)
last_period_end <- max(pci_data$period_end)

# Create a lookup for the eventual names of the metrics
lookup_colnames <- c(
  "Number of PCI, n" = "label_pci",
  "Number of STEMIs, n (%)" = "label_stemi",
  "Radial Access, n (%)" = "label_radial",
  "Mean Length of Stay" = "label_mean_los",
  "Median Length of Stay" = "label_median_los"
)

summary_latest <- pci_data_for_stratified_tables |> 
  # Apply filters
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(age) & !is.na(inds_cat) & !is.na(acs_cat)) |>
  dplyr::filter(period_end == last_period_end) |>
  # Group By
  dplyr::group_by(label_comparison_group = comparison_group) |>
  # Calculate required metrics (for eventual rows)
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_pci = sum(count_pci),
    n_stemi = sum(dplyr::if_else(acs_cat == "STEMI", 1, 0)),
    n_radial = sum(dplyr::if_else(access_route == "Radial", 1, 0)),
    mean_los = mean(los_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_los = median(los_median, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    label_pci = formatC(n_pci, big.mark = ","),
    label_stemi = paste0(formatC(n_stemi, big.mark = ","), " (", round(n_stemi/n_pci * 100, 0), "%)"),
    label_radial = paste0(formatC(n_radial, big.mark = ","), " (", round(n_radial/n_pci * 100, 0), "%)"),
    label_mean_los = paste0(formatC(mean_los, digits = 1, format = "f"), " days"),
    label_median_los = paste0(round(median_los, 0), " ", dplyr::if_else(median_los == 1, "day", "days"))
  ) |>
  # Rename columns to meaningful names
  dplyr::rename(
    all_of(lookup_colnames)
  ) |>
  # Only select required columns
  dplyr::select(
    label_comparison_group,
    names(lookup_colnames)
  ) |>
  # Transpose table
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -label_comparison_group, names_to = "Metric", values_to = "value") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "label_comparison_group", values_from = value, names_sort = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(Metric, sort(tidyselect::peek_vars(), decreasing = TRUE))

# Format flextable output
header_span_name <- dplyr::case_when(
  params$period_frequency == 'monthly' ~ paste0(format.Date(last_period_end, "%b %Y")),
  params$period_frequency == 'quarterly' ~ paste0(format.Date(last_period_start, "%b %Y"), " to ", format.Date(last_period_end, "%b %Y")),
  .default = "Missing Period Frequency"
)

summary_latest |>
  flextable::flextable() |>
  flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 0.7) |>
  flextable::theme_box() |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") |>
  flextable::padding(padding = 2, part = "all") |>
  flextable::align(j = 1, align = "left", part = "all") |>
  flextable::align(j = 2:3, align = "center", part = "all") |>
  flextable::add_header_row(values = c("", header_span_name), colwidths = c(1, 2)) |>
  flextable::set_header_labels("Metric" = "")
```

# Patient Demographics (`r short_report_start_date` to `r short_report_end_date`)

## Patient Characteristics by Clinical Presentation

```{r stat_ggplot2_function, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
stat_ggplot2 <- function(data, stat, title, x_axis_short_label, show_legend = FALSE) {
  # Calculate Required Statistics for ggplot visual
  stat_data <- rbind(
    data |>
      dplyr::group_by(comparison_group, acs_cat) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        stat = {{stat}}
      ),
    data |>
      dplyr::group_by(comparison_group) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        stat = {{stat}}
      ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        acs_cat = "All"
      )
  ) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from = comparison_group,
      values_from = stat
    ) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      stat_target = `Your Data`,
      stat_all = `All PCI Operators`
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      acs_cat = factor(acs_cat, levels = c("Elective/Other", "ACS", "STEMI", "All"))
    )
  
  # Calculate ggplot2 x-axis range
  min_point <- min(c(stat_data$stat_target, stat_data$stat_other), na.rm = TRUE)
  max_point <- max(c(stat_data$stat_target, stat_data$stat_other), na.rm = TRUE)
  range <- max_point - min_point
  min_range <- min_point - range * 0.15
  max_range <- max_point + range * 0.15
  
  # Initialise ggplot chart
  ggplot2_output <- ggplot2::ggplot(stat_data) +
    # Add horizontal bars for Your Data
    ggplot2::geom_bar(
      ggplot2::aes(
        y = acs_cat,
        x = stat_target,
        fill = "Your Data"
      ),
      stat = "identity"
    ) +
    # Add points for Other Clinician average
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      ggplot2::aes(
        y = acs_cat,
        x = stat_all,
        color = "All PCI Operators",
        shape = "All PCI Operators"
      ),
      size = 8
    ) +
    # Add y axis label
    ggplot2::ylab("") +
    # Add x axis label
    ggplot2::xlab(x_axis_short_label) +
    # Set x-axis limits
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(min_range, max_range)
    ) +
    # Add title
    ggplot2::ggtitle(title) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 16,
                                         face = "bold", family = "sans",
                                         margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 0)),
      # panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      # panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, color = "#000000"),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, color = "#000000")
    ) +
    # Set manual color and shapes by group names
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
      name = "", 
      breaks = c("Your Data"),
      values = c("Your Data" = "#00667B")
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
      name = "", 
      breaks = c("All PCI Operators"),
      values = c("All PCI Operators" = "#000000")
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
      name = "", 
      values = c("All PCI Operators" = 108)
    ) +
    # Format Legend
    ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position = ifelse(show_legend, "bottom", "none"), 
      legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 14)
    ) +
    ggplot2::guides(
      fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(order = 1)
    )
  
  return(ggplot2_output)
}
```

```{r demographics_by_acs_table, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
demographic_tbl_summary <- function(data) {
  data |>
    gtsummary::tbl_summary(
      include = c(age, severe_obesity, ppci, pcabg, db, pvd, los_mean, los_median, los_cat),
      by = "comparison_group",
      label = list(
        age ~ "Age",
        severe_obesity ~ "Severe Obesity (BMI ≥ 35 kg/m²)",
        ppci ~ "Previous PCI",
        pcabg ~ "Previous CABG",
        db ~ "Diabetic",
        pvd ~ "Peripheral Vascular Disease",
        los_mean ~ "Average Length of Stay (Mean)",
        los_median ~ "Average Length of Stay (Median)",
        los_cat ~ "Length of Stay"
      ),
      statistic = list(
        c(age, los_mean) ~ "{mean}",
        c(los_median) ~ "{median}",
        c(severe_obesity, ppci, pcabg, db, pvd, los_cat) ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
      ),
      digits = list(
        c(age) ~ 1,
        c(los_mean) ~ 1,
        c(los_median) ~ 0
      ),
      missing = "no"
    )
}

tbl_stratified_and_overall <- function(data, func_tbl_summary, label_name = "Characteristic") {
  # Create a stratified table by ACS category
  tbl_stratified <- data |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      acs_cat_factor = factor(acs_cat, levels = c("STEMI", "ACS", "Elective/Other"), ordered = TRUE)
    ) |>
    gtsummary::tbl_strata(
      strata = "acs_cat_factor",
      .tbl_fun = 
        ~ .x |>
        func_tbl_summary()
    )
  
  # Create an overall table for all PCI
  tbl_overall <- data |>
    func_tbl_summary() |> 
    gtsummary::modify_spanning_header(gtsummary::all_stat_cols() ~ "**All PCI**")
  
  # Merge the stratified and overall tables
  ft_tbl <- list(tbl_stratified, tbl_overall) |>
    gtsummary::tbl_merge(tab_spanner = FALSE) |>
    # Change label name for first column
    gtsummary::modify_header(label ~ paste0("**", label_name, "**")) |>
    # Force the header to split into two lines with the N = {n} on the second line
    gtsummary::modify_header(gtsummary::all_stat_cols() ~ "**{level}** \nN = {n}") |>
    gtsummary::as_flex_table()
  
  # Format the flextable
  ft_tbl_modified <- ft_tbl |>
    # fit size to whole screen
    flextable::autofit() |>
    # background colour
    flextable::bg(part = "header", bg = "#00667B") |>
    # text colour
    flextable::color(part = "header", color = "white") |>
    flextable::bold(part = "header") |>
    # Bold last two columns
    flextable::bold(j = 8:9) |>
    # Fill last two columns
    flextable::bg(j = 8:9, bg = "#D9D9D9") |>
    # Borders between clinical indications by column
    flextable::border(i = 1:(nrow(ft_tbl$body$dataset)), j = c(1,3,5,7,9), border.right = officer::fp_border(color = "black"), part = "body") |>
    flextable::border(j = c(1,3,5,7,9), border.right = officer::fp_border(color = "black"), part = "header") |>
    flextable::border(i = 1:(nrow(ft_tbl$body$dataset)), j = c(2,4,6,8), border.right = officer::fp_border(color = "#A6A6A6"), part = "body") |>
    flextable::border(j = c(2,4,6,8), border.right = officer::fp_border(color = "#A6A6A6"), part = "header") |>
    # Borders between clinical indications by column
    flextable::border(i = 1:(nrow(ft_tbl$body$dataset)), j = 1, border.left = officer::fp_border(color = "black"), part = "body") |>
    flextable::border(j = 1, border.left = officer::fp_border(color = "black"), part = "header") |>
    # Font sizes
    flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
    flextable::padding(padding = 1, part = "all") |>
    flextable::align(j = 1, align = "left", part = "all") |>
    flextable::align(j = 2:9, align = "center", part = "all") |>
    flextable::valign(j = 2:9, valign = "center", part = "all") |>
    # Width of cells
    flextable::width(j = 1, width = 4.96, unit = "cm") |>
    flextable::width(j = 2:9, width = 1.87, unit = "cm")
  
  if (nrow(ft_tbl$body$dataset) > 1) {
    ft_tbl_modified <- ft_tbl_modified |>
      # Borders between rows
      flextable::border(i = 1:(nrow(ft_tbl$body$dataset)-1), border.bottom = officer::fp_border(color = "#A6A6A6"), part = "body")
  }
  
  return(ft_tbl_modified)
}

tbl_stratified_and_overall(
  pci_data_for_stratified_tables |> 
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(age) & !is.na(inds_cat) & !is.na(acs_cat)) |>
    # Add spacing in front of group for formatting
    dplyr::mutate(los_cat = factor(los_cat, labels = paste0("    ", levels(pci_data$los_cat)))), 
  demographic_tbl_summary
)
```

## 30-Day Mortality After PCI

# Appendix

## Definitions

### Clinical Presentation

The tables and bar charts in this report are stratified by the patient's clinical presentation in the 7 day period leading up to and including the index PCI. These categories are:

- ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI),
- Acute Coronary Syndromes (ACS), and 
- Elective/Other.

The ACS group is equivalent to the NCR non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTEACS) group, and Elective/Other is equivalent to the NCR Non-ACS group as reported in the NCR Annual Report.

### NCR QI3: In-Hospital Stroke
**Description:** Proportion of patients that undergo a PCI procedure that experienced a stroke while an inpatient during or after the cardiac catheter lab visit.

**Denominator:** Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure.

**Numerator:** Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure and experienced a stroke or new central neurologic deficit (persisting for > 72 hours) during the cardiac catheter lab visit, after the lab visit, but prior to discharge and/or any subsequent lab visits.

### 30-Day Stroke Post Discharge
**Description:** Proportion of patients that undergo a PCI procedure that had a new stroke during the 30-day follow-up period after discharge from hospital.

**Denominator:** Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure and were discharged from hospital alive.

**Numerator:** Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure and were admitted into hospital for Stroke within 30 days of discharge from hospital. The stroke admission can be either to the emergency department or to an inpatient bed.

### NCR QI6: 30-Day Cardiac Rehospitalisation
**Description:** Proportion of patients that undergo a PCI procedure that had cardiac rehospitalisation within 30 days after discharge from hospital.

**Denominator:** Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure and were discharged from hospital alive.

**Numerator:** Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure and had a cardiac rehospitalisation within 30 days of discharge, where a cardiac rehospitalisation is defined as an in-patient admission that includes, but is not limited to any of the following circumstances: heart failure; acute coronary syndrome (e.g. STEMI, ACS; recurrent or unstable angina); arrhythmia; elective (non emergency) PCI or CABG etc.


### NCR QI8: 30-Day Mortality After PCI
**Description:** Proportion of patients that undergo a PCI procedure that died in-hospital or within 30 days of discharge.  

**Denominator:** Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure.

**Numerator:** Number of procedures that undergo a PCI procedure with a discharge status of death or death within 30 days of discharge.


\newpage

## Reporting Format

The data is presented using tables, bar plots, statistical process control (SPC) charts for individual clinician data, and funnel plots where each point represents an individual clinician over the reporting period, with the Your Data annotated in the funnel plot (e.g. Q5 below).

All clinicians are displayed in a funnel plot (left) and for Your Data by an SPC chart (right).

```{r example_funnel_spc, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Example funnel plot using simulated data
set.seed(12345)
set_marker_sample_fp1 <- sample(1:25)
denom <- sapply(1:5, function(x) rpois(5, x * 20)) |> c()
numer <- (sapply(1:5, function(x) rpois(5, x * 20 * 0.7)) |> c() -
       (runif(25) * 10) |> round(0)) |> sapply(function(x) ifelse(x < 0, 0, x))
fp_data <- data.table::data.table(
  num = numer,
  den = denom,
  prop = numer/denom*100,
  hospital_name = paste0("Q", 1:25),
  hospital_group_name = paste0("Q", 1:25)
)

controlcharts_funnel(
  data = fp_data,
  numerator = num,
  denominator = den,
  group = hospital_name,
  group_name = hospital_group_name,
  title = "Example Funnel Plot",
  labels = "Q5",
  chart_type = "PR",
  height = 340,
  width = 370,
  improvement_direction = "increase",
  ylimit_label = "Proportion (%)",
  xlimit_label = "Number of cases"
)

# Example SPC using simulated data
spc_data <- data.table::data.table(
  month = seq(from = as.Date("2021-03-01"),
          to = as.Date("2024-05-01"),
          by = "month") - 1,
  numerator = c(21, 13, 16, 15, 7, 10, 22, 18, 18, 30, 29, 18, 23, 17, 18,
                15, 17, 19, 21, 30, 19, 15, 17, 22, 24, 20, 10,
                6, 18, 14, 21, 17, 27, 24, 30, 25, 24, 26, 24),
  denominator = c(96, 93, 87, 86, 91, 99, 110, 96, 110, 96, 97, 105, 87, 94, 89,
                  102, 106, 107, 95, 106, 132, 95, 117, 97, 99, 108, 106,
                  101, 96, 96, 98, 105, 117, 94, 77, 97, 90, 106, 107)
)
controlcharts_spc(
  data = spc_data,
  numerator = numerator,
  denominator = denominator,
  month = month,
  height = 340,
  width = 370,
  chart_type = "p",
  improvement_direction = "decrease",
  xlimit_label = "Months",
  ylimit_label = NULL,
  title = "Example SPC Chart Your Data",
  upper_padding = 15
)
```

Multiple elements comprise the funnel plots and SPC charts:

* 2 sigma (2σ) limits are displayed as dotted lines, representing 95% warning limits
* 3 sigma (3σ) limits are displayed as dashed lines, representing 99.8% control limits
* dark solid line represents the centreline, indicating the mean value of observed counts for a given KPI at the named hospital
* blue dot represents improvement or a favourable direction for a specific KPI
* orange dot represents an unfavourable pattern for a specific KPI
* grey dot in the SPC chart represents the actual observed value
* grey dot in the funnel plot denotes the clinicians included in the analysis

The table below summarises the SPC patterns and their symbols that are annotated on the above chart.

```{r pattern_id_table, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE, quiet=TRUE, results = "asis"}
#table describing patterns and their symbols
col1 <- c("Pattern", "SPC - Astronomical Point", "SPC - Trend (5)",
          "SPC - Two in Three", "SPC - Shift (7)")
col2 <- c("Pattern Symbol", "\u2252", "\u24e3", "\u2154", "\u24e2")
col3 <- c(
  "Pattern summary",
  "An identified point that exceeds three sigma limits from the mean",
  "Five consecutively increasing or decreasing points",
  "Two out of Three consecutive points exceeding two sigma limits from the mean", # nolint
  "Seven consecutive points above or below the mean"
)
create_table <- function(...) {
  # binds the vectors into dataframe
  output <- data.frame(...)
  # takes first item in vector and makes it the column name
  colnames(output) <- output[1, ]
  # removes repeated row
  output <- output[-1, ]
  return(output)
}
pattern_id_table <- create_table(col1, col2, col3)
pattern_id_table |>
  # Create flextable
  flextable::flextable() |>
  # Set layout to stretch and autofit across the page
  flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1) |>
  # Make header bold
  flextable::bold(part = "header") |>
  # Add vertical line between columns
  flextable::border_inner_v() |>
  # Set font size to 10 for the entire table
  flextable::fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") |>
  # Remove padding for entire table
  flextable::padding(padding = 0, part = "all")
```

The NHS icon (located at top right corner of the SPC chart) summarises the SPC pattern for the latest data point in the chart. An orange icon indicates an unfavourable pattern, a blue icon indicates an favourable pattern and a grey icon indicates common cause variation.

Detailed guidance on the Making Data Count approach can be found on the [Making Data Count website](https://www.england.nhs.uk/ourwork/innovation/making-data-count/), and WA DoH HQIU's [Understanding our Charts guide](https://wahealthdept.sharepoint.com/:p:/r/sites/SafetyandQualityIndicatorSetSQuIS/Shared%20Documents/Guides%20and%20web%20documents/User%20Guides/Understanding%20our%20charts.pptx?d=wadb9facb07f244219cfed745082104f5&csf=1&web=1&e=Umf2cJ).
